top_issues: Promised vs Reserve meaning lives only in the small 12px legend under the total bar; the violet/green bars carry the whole risk story and are unreadable without squinting (Home, lower-left).
Receive/Swap buttons render as dark bordered cards and read as disabled next to the filled indigo Pay; a first-timer can't tell two of three primary actions are live.
Large empty mid-left area between Balances and the left rail; the page breathes but wastes the strongest screen real estate.
fixes: Promote the green/violet legend to a persistent 14px control directly under the balance bar, and open it on hover to explain 'enforceable vs promised'.
Give Receive/Swap a visible indigo outline or lighter fill so they read as actionable next to Pay.
Pull the Accounts/Recent cards tighter to the left to fill the dead zone, or reduce the left rail height.

top_issues: The route copy 'forwards atomically fee 0.000025 of 0.000050 total' is dense and reads as legal; a lay user can't tell the fee from the route.
The 'Provable' card and the before/after H1 bars add two extra reading passes before the Pay button; the critical 'nothing moves on-chain' claim is buried.
Fee and Arrives rows use small gray labels that drop contrast on the near-black background.
fixes: Split the route line into plain 'Fee' and 'Arrives in' rows with one fee number each; move the 0.000025 internal split into an expandable detail.
Promote the Provable assertion to a single inline chip above the Pay button: 'Signed both sides, nothing on-chain'.
Raise label color from ~#8B8B93 to #B5B5BF for the fee/arrives rows.

top_issues: The proof hash and frame number are the only 'receipt' data a forwardable customer sees; a non-technical recipient (Sofia's client) won't know what to do with 0x4dd62f8.
'Verified by your runtime' is jargon to an outsider.
No explicit 'shared / forwarded' affordance — only Copy and Download, no 'send to recipient'.
fixes: Add a human summary line 'Paid to H2 via H1, settled in 8s' and offer a 'Forward to recipient' button that generates a clean, non-technical receipt.
Replace 'Verified by your runtime' with 'Signed and verifiable on-chain'.
Keep the frame/proof row but tuck it under a 'Technical details' disclosure.

top_issues: Three disconnected columns (QR, share, entity id) scatter the task; a first-timer doesn't know which element to act on first.
'Prepare incoming account / H1-Testnet / capacity is checked' is pure protocol jargon with no plain-language reason.
'Your ENTITY ID' with a long hex string is intimidating and unexplained.
fixes: Reorder into a single vertical flow: QR -> amount -> 'who can pay this' -> share; move the Entity ID into a collapsed 'Technical' section.
Rewrite the capacity line as 'Up to 48.00 USDC can arrive through H1' with a link to add more capacity.
Label the entity id as 'Your wallet address on xln'.

top_issues: Busiest screen: order book, collateral slider, credit note, and the primary action all compete; scroll required to reach 'Swap USDC for WETH'.
Primary 'Swap USDC for WETH' button is muted indigo and reads as disabled until it scrolls into view.
No explicit fill/slippage line — 'receive 0.039992' is a quote, not a record of what a fill cost; Anya can't see her real slippage.
The '100% collateral -> 0%' slider maps to two different scales and takes a beat to parse.
fixes: Make the Swap button fully saturated indigo and pin it as the visible primary action, not below the fold.
Add a 'fills + slippage' line under the receive amount once an order fills.
Add a one-line plain note next to the slider: '0 collateral = your credit cap is consumed first'.
Split the three columns into two with the order book collapsed behind a toggle.

top_issues: The four-color legend row (secured vs promised vs credit room vs in flight) is tiny and easy to miss, yet it defines the whole risk model.
'credit room' appears only in the legend, not as a number; Marcus wants a single exposure figure per hub.
'Show 1 empty lane: USDT' at the bottom is an odd orphan note that breaks the visual flow.
fixes: Turn the legend into a 14px toggleable control and surface 'credit room' as an explicit value per lane.
Add a per-hub 'net exposure' figure in the 'THIS ACCOUNT' panel summing lines out minus the other side.
Move the empty-lane note into a small muted line inside the lane section, not a stray sentence.

top_issues: The detail panel already shows the selected row in the list, so the list and detail feel like one long panel rather than two distinct views.
No filter by counterparty or date range, which a treasurer (Ravi) needs to build an audit ledger.
Status chips (filled/open/settled) use subtle dots that lose meaning at a glance.
fixes: Add a counterparty and date-range filter row under 'All / Payments / Swaps'.
Make status chips include a short word + color, not just a dot + word, and increase contrast.
Add an 'Export' dropdown with CSV for the current filter to support audit exports.

top_issues: This appears to be a near-duplicate of 07-activity; the 'detail' view adds no materially different layout, so the set provides no real detail-level review.
The detail panel asserts '2 committed entries' without showing the individual entries, so proof is opaque.
No independent 'detail' affordance — the same drawer is open in both screens.
fixes: Make the detail panel actually expandable to list the 2 committed frames with hashes and times.
Differentiate the detail view visually (e.g., a standalone route instead of the list + reflection) so it reads as a distinct screen.
Add a 'view full proof' link opening the evidence bundle.

top_issues: Very dense small-text list; the nested 'AT THIS SCALE / 1px = $1' demo with $1,284,500.00 is excellent but the surrounding rows are cramped.
The 'Forget vault' destructive action in red-orange sits in the same visual weight as 'Lock', risking accidental clicks.
The bar-scale control is powerful but there's no live preview of how 1px = $1 vs $10 changes real lanes; a user can't see the effect on their actual data.
fixes: Group settings into collapsible sections with more padding and larger row labels.
Separate destructive actions into a muted 'Danger zone' with a confirm step.
Add a live mini-preview of the current user's lanes at the chosen px value.

top_issues: The From/To card grids show balances but the per-card bars are tiny and inconsistent in scale, so the 'source of funds' comparison is harder than it needs to be.
'Sign & send' vs 'Add to batch' — the primary is filled but the batch action is a second, equally prominent button that competes.
The 'up to 40.00 USDC' constraint appears below the amount rather than on the source card, so a user discovers the limit late.
fixes: Raise the per-card bar contrast and align all cards to one absolute scale with a shared 'max' reference.
Demote 'Add to batch' to a smaller, visually secondary control.
Move the source-capacity limit onto the selected From card as 'max 40.00'.

top_issues: Large empty bottom-right area; the ACCOUNTS card floats top-right leaving the lower half of the screen dead.
'WHERE YOUR MONEY STANDS' is the best element but sits mid-page; the empty 'NEEDS ATTENTION: nothing waiting on you' wastes prime space.
The navigation cards (Sovereignty / Move / Assets / Lending) have uneven sizes and no hierarchy of importance.
fixes: Fill the dead space with a recent-activity or per-hub exposure preview, or make the money stand a hero panel.
Give the overview and attention sections equal width so the page composition is balanced.
Standardize the nav card grid to equal heights and add a short one-line description under each title.

top_issues: The right column is a two-in-one 'Faucets' + 'Prepare to receive' panel that mixes a dev/test tool with the real asset flow; unusual for a production wallet.
The 'Extend credit limit' primary button is muted indigo and reads as disabled.
Gas shows as '0.1000 ETH' but there's no fee/network context, and the signer/depository addresses have no 'copy' affordance visible.
fixes: Separate the dev/test 'Faucets' into a clearly gated 'Testnet tools' section with a warning, and keep the real flow clean.
Saturate the Extend-credit button and make the primary action unambiguous.
Add copy icons next to the signer and depository addresses.

top_issues: The '=100% per term' derived from 100 bps is confusing — a user may read it as 100% interest.
'Offer to the pool' is muted indigo and reads as disabled even though it's the page's primary action.
The H1 POOL panel shows zeros for everything, which reads as 'no data' rather than an empty state explanation.
fixes: Render the interest as '1.00% per term' and show the bps in a sub-label, not the reverse.
Saturate the 'Offer to the pool' button to full indigo.
Add an empty-state line: 'No active pool yet — your offer creates it.'

top_issues: Very sparse: one board card plus an empty 'take control' card on a mostly blank page; reads as unfinished.
The two explanatory paragraphs of legal text under 'Kind' are dense and low-contrast.
No evidence of the signer's role or what a 'rotation' would change — the value of this screen is unclear.
fixes: Condense the board explanation into a short summary and add a small 'what a rotation does' demo or visual.
Add a list of signers/quorum and a 'rotate key' preview so the screen has a purpose.
Fill the right column with ownership-history or pending-rotation info instead of an empty card.

top_issues: 'Save evidence bundle' is the key audit action but there's no preview of what's in the bundle (which frames/accounts) before saving.
The PER COUNTERPARTY card, which shows $122.99 at risk, is the most important trust element but is pushed to the top-right, under-competing with the hero balance.
Left column runs long while the right column ends early, creating asymmetric whitespace.
fixes: Add an expandable bundle contents list under 'Save evidence bundle' so the user sees exactly what is exported.
Move the per-counterparty risk card to sit right beside the hero, or give it equal visual weight.
Balance the columns by adding a 'what you can prove' summary under the ledger.

top_issues: Dense two-column terminal; excellent for Marcus but the order book + lane table compete, and a newcomer has no entry point.
Legend row (on-chain / reserve / secured / promised / you owe / credit room) is the only key to the four-color lanes and it's a thin 11-12px strip.
No aggregate 'net exposure / total at risk' figure per lane, only per-cell values; a hub operator has to sum manually.
fixes: Add a collapsible 'first-time explainer' banner and a persistent larger legend that expands on hover.
Add a 'net exposure' column per lane and a total at-risk footer.
Provide a 'simplify' toggle to hide the order book for non-pro users.

top_issues: The palette overlay is clean and keyboard-friendly, but the temptation to jump via ⌘K makes the primary nav feel secondary.
The shortcut hints ('send money', 'invoice OR', 'batch attention doors') are cryptic and inconsistent in style.
Palette items use icon+label+subtitle; the subtitle text is low-contrast and hard to scan quickly.
fixes: Normalize the subtitle copy to short plain phrases ('Send money', 'Create invoice', 'Review pending actions').
Raise subtitle contrast and align all subtitles to the same column.
Keep ⌘K as a power-user shortcut but ensure the sidebar nav remains the visible primary path.

overall.verdict: A disciplined, confident dark UI that solves the hardest problem in the product — it separates enforceable from promised money at one absolute scale and makes counterparty risk readable in seconds, with unusually strong trust signals (signed frames, evidence bundle, request-receipt). The wasted opportunity is reach: no mobile proof, a few sparse/under-designed pages, weak primary-button affordance on action screens, and missing task flows (invoice, cross-network fee breakdown, per-fill slippage) that would unlock four of the ten personas.
priority_fixes: Ship mobile screens and a single-column one-hand flow for Pay/Receive; the multi-column desktop layouts cannot pass Lena's 10-second checkout.
Make the primary action unambiguous everywhere — Swap, Extend credit, Offer to the pool currently render muted-indigo and read as disabled.
Elevate the promised-vs-enforceable legend from a 12px strip into a first-class, persistent 14px hero explainer on Home/Desk.
Add the missing task flows: a real Create-invoice screen (Sofia), a per-leg cross-network fee breakdown (Fatima), and per-fill/slippage history in Swap (Anya).
Fill the sparse empty states (Ownership 14, Manage 11) with the data users need — evidence-bundle preview on Sovereignty and a net-exposure sum per hub on Account/Desk.

personas.name: Maya
personas.verdict: I could probably pay a friend — the big number and Pay button are obvious — but 'Reserve', 'Promised', 'credit line' and 'entity id' started sounding like a bank I don't understand, and I'd freeze at 'Prepare incoming account'.
blockers: Receive (04): 'Prepare incoming account / H1-Testnet / capacity is checked' and 'Your ENTITY ID' are jargon with no plain-language why.
Home (01): the violet/green bars need the small legend to mean anything; 'Promised $147.99' is opaque without it.
Pay (02): the Provable card reads like legal text to a first-timer.

personas.name: Tomasz
personas.verdict: I can read my credit line vs collateral in seconds on the Account and Desk views — the fastest bilateral-risk read I've had, once I find the legend.
blockers: Account (06): the four-color legend (secured vs promised vs credit room vs in flight) is a thin, easily-missed strip that carries the whole risk story.
Swap (05): the '100% collateral -> 0%' slider takes a beat to map to real numbers.
Desk (16): no net exposure figure per lane; I sum manually.

personas.name: Anya
personas.verdict: The order book is legible and the price ladder is real, but I can't see my actual fills or slippage, and the swap is buried behind an unusual collateral-extension step.
blockers: Swap (05): no fills/slippage line — 'receive 0.039992' is a quote, not a fill record; Activity (07/08) shows 'swap placed' as open with no fill price.
Swap (05): primary 'Swap USDC for WETH' is muted-indigo and reads as disabled until scrolled.
Swap (05): the credit-limit collateral step is a DEX-unfamiliar gate that adds friction to a fair-price trade.

personas.name: Ravi
personas.verdict: This is the one product that tells me exactly what is enforceable right now versus promised and hands me a signed evidence bundle — that is board-report ready.
blockers: Sovereignty (15): 'Save evidence bundle' exists but no preview of the bundle contents before saving, and no obvious 'export for the board'.
Home (01)/Desk (16): enforceable vs promised is top-level but reconciling to specific lanes requires cross-referencing the Desk.
Activity (07): no filter by counterparty/date range to build a clean audit ledger.

personas.name: Sofia
personas.verdict: I can get paid and there's a beautiful receipt, but there is no invoice screen — nothing to send a client with an amount and my details — so I'm still doing invoices elsewhere.
blockers: No invoice screen in the set; the closest is Receive (04), which has amount + note but no client name, due date, invoice number, or branded PDF.
Receive (04): the only share path is a payment link/QR; no professional invoice template.
Receipt (03): the receipt is internal (frame, proof hash) — a non-technical client wants a clean 'Invoice # paid' summary.

personas.name: Kenji
personas.verdict: The Dispute path, evidence bundle, and 'can dispute without asking' plus frame hashes are exactly what I want — I just need the challenge-window timer and the full bundle visible before I commit.
blockers: Account (06)/Manage (11): 'Dispute' is a button, but the challenge window (how long I have) and evidence bundle contents aren't shown.
Sovereignty (15): the bundle is saved but no preview of which frames/accounts are inside.
Home (01): the 'Promised' amount has no one-click 'see why' to drill into the risk.

personas.name: Lena
personas.verdict: I only got desktop screens and they're dense — if this doesn't compress to one thumb-friendly view on a phone, I'm out; the two-column layouts and tiny legend rows won't survive.
blockers: No mobile screens in the set; every screen (Home, Pay, Swap, Desk) is multi-column and assumes a big display.
Home (01): balance bar + legend + recent list is too much for a one-hand checkout; tap targets are unproven for thumbs.
Pay (02): route line + Provable card add steps; 10 seconds requires one amount pre-set and a single confirm.

personas.name: Marcus
personas.verdict: The Desk and Account views give me lines-out, collateral, and send/receive capacity at one absolute scale — the clearest counterparty-exposure read in the market.
blockers: Desk (16): the lane table is excellent but no net-position or aggregate-exposure summary per counterparty beyond single lanes.
Account (06): 'credit room' is only in the legend, not as a number; I want one exposure figure per hub.
Settings (09): the bar-scale control is powerful but there's no preview of how it affects real small lanes.

personas.name: Fatima
personas.verdict: I can route through H1 and the fee is visible, but there's no cross-network path or per-leg fee breakdown, and I'm not sure the number I see is the total.
blockers: Pay (02)/Swap (05): the route shows only the internal hub fee split; no per-leg fee breakdown or total across networks.
No cross-network/bridge screen in the set; 'Across networks' tab exists in Swap (05) but no cross-network flow is shown.
Home (01): 'Instantly receive up to $25.80' is a capacity constraint that would block a large cross-border transfer.

personas.name: Dmitri
personas.verdict: In three minutes I understand this is a credit-based, self-custodial wallet where 'promised' is honestly separated from 'enforceable' — that honesty is the differentiator — but the trust story is buried in tiny legend text.
blockers: Home (01): the green/violet legend is small; the core innovation (one scale, promised vs enforceable) should be a visible hero explainer.
Settings (09): 'Risk color' and 'Accent' customization suggests the trust semantics are skin-deep, slightly undercutting the safety story.
Sovereignty (15): the 'enforceable right now $40.00' hero is good, but the 'why safe' narrative isn't told on the first screen.
